Kazuma Kiryu, the legendary dragon, needs no introduction. His dominating presence is well known to every fighter who has set foot in the Underground Coliseum. He is a living legend and has left an indelible mark in this ring.

Though Akiyama has a brief history here at the Underground Coliseum, his impressive record speaks for itself. Legions of fans have been captivated by his footwork. However, he never seems all that eager to participate.

Saejima's claim to infamy is in taking out 18 yakuza in a single bloody hit at a ramen shop. He is known to beat his opponents into the ground with overwhelming power. Lesser known is the massive damage his bouts deal to the ring and the extensive repairs required.

Once a talented batter, Shinada has faded into obscurity since his glory days. It is unclear why he has entered the ring here in the Underground Coliseum, but after making his way through the Victory Road qualifier, his fighting prowess is abundantly clear.
Once considered the emperor of the Underground Coliseum, nobody knows why he left, nor why he has returned now. The only thing for certain is that he is still the strongest, and he is out for blood.

A masked man of unknown origins, it is said that staring into his eyes through the mask will shorten your life, and just a glimpse of his maskless face means death. Those who fight him fight against fate.
This superhuman knows not defeat, having supposedly faked all of his losses. His unparalleled physique alone is enough to make even the most hardened fighter think twice about fighting him.

Adabana once conquered the sumo world, surpassing the greatest the sport had ever known, and he became known as the New Legend. However, after breaking an opponent's neck with a single blow, he was forced to retire at the peak of his career.

Once per generation, no matter the place, a person of great talent emerges. Their skill is so great that the only explanation can be that they were blessed by the gods. In the Underground Coliseum, Ginga is that person.

An enigma shrouded in mystery. Who is he really, and why is he fighting in the Coliseum? He has downed a multitude of opponents with his iron-hard fists, said to be blessed by the unholy power of the Devil himself. He is the strongest man alive.

Master martial artist and founder of Komaki school of martial arts. His unusually strong physique continues to improve and evolve as he ages. He has come to the Coliseum to challenge himself and to promote the Komaki style.

The successor of the Hozoin spear technique, passed down from the Azuchi-Momoyama Period. His superior spear skills and fluid movements are on par with those of the style's founder, Inei. He fights to spread the Hozoin spirit.
A former star of action films which featured real fighting, his life turned to tragedy and despair when he went beyond acting and killed a co-star.

A mysterious man with a reputation for using everyday items like business cards, pens, and watches as deadly weapons. He is forbidden from exchanging business cards with other fighters for this reason.

A masked fighter with a history of unspeakable acts in the pro wrestling ring. He came to the Underground Coliseum looking for a fight, but he also seeks an opportunity to get revenge on those in the pro wrestling world against whom he holds a burning grudge.
